svg.title: Service worker update lifecycle
svg.desc: A deploy changes sw.js. The browser checks the script on navigation, and on push or sync events if it has not checked in the last 24 hours, ignoring the HTTP cache by default, and installs the new worker if the script is byte-different. The new worker moves through four states: installing, where the install event precaches the v2 files; waiting, because v1 still controls the open tabs; activating, where the activate event deletes old caches; and activated, where v2 controls new page loads. Three ways lead out of waiting. One: wait for every tab to close, the default and safest, because no page runs with a mismatched worker, although one tab left open can delay it for days. Two: prompt, then reload: the page shows Update available, on click it posts a message and the worker calls skipWaiting, and on controllerchange the page reloads once. Three: call skipWaiting during install, the fastest, but v2 activates at once and, with clients.claim, controls pages loaded by v1, mixing versions. A note says long-open tabs should call registration.update on an interval such as hourly, sw.js should be served with Cache-Control no-cache, and old hashed assets should stay on the server for pages still running v1. A new service worker waits by design; skipping the wait trades safety for speed.
